disclaimer: Timings and magnitudes are rough real-world approximations for teaching. Problems may override any param.

fieldGuide.group: traffic | data | infra | dependency | change | security | cost | compliance
fieldGuide.severity: 1 mild, 2 serious, 3 severe. Drives the warning sound and banner colour.
fieldGuide.effects: Ordered list of engine ops applied when the event starts. See 'ops'.
fieldGuide.target: Selector string. See 'selectors'. A problem may override it with params.target.
fieldGuide.untilFixed: The effect lasts until people notice and fix it: detection time plus repair time from world.json 'response', which depends on the observability and control elements present.
fieldGuide.counters: Elements or knobs that soften the event. The engine applies these through ordinary behaviour; the list drives the debrief and hints.
fieldGuide.debrief: Plain-words templates. Placeholders in braces are filled by sim results (see CONTRACT.md, DebriefData).
fieldGuide.realWorld: One sentence tying the event to the real world, with approximate numbers.

selectors.kind:<kind>: Every element of that kind, for example kind:store.
selectors.el:<elementId>: Every placed element of that type, for example el:sql-primary.
selectors.cat:<category>: Every element in that category, for example cat:external.
selectors.busiest:<kind|el:id|cat:id>: The single placed element of that group with the highest utilisation when the event starts.
selectors.random:<kind|el:id|cat:id>: One placed element of that group chosen by the seeded random generator.
selectors.keyed: Every placed element whose params.keyed is true, plus caches.
selectors.ref:<nodeRef>: A specific node from the problem starter or editorial.

params.types: optional list of request types; default all

params.factorOfPeak: attack rps as a multiple of the problem's peak rps
params.types: request types it imitates for routing

params.share: share of users moved to that region
share of a keyed element's traffic that lands on one unit or key

params.factor: multiplier on writes reaching stores and queues

params.recoverSec: seconds for the hit rate to return; coalesce on the cache divides misses reaching the origin by 10

params.durationSec: seconds; the seeded random generator picks zone a, b or c

params.lagSec: replication or copy lag in seconds

params.durationSec: seconds; callers with backoff 'none' re-send failed requests up to their retries count in the next tick

params.checks: list of compliance check ids from world.json 'complianceChecks'

params.perHour: share of capacity lost per hour

params.durationSec: untilFixed; consumers of the target queue process nothing unless a dead-letter queue is connected
seconds; regions cannot reach each other

params.rpsCapFactor: new capacity as a share of the target's current load

params.share: share of rows damaged; replicas copy the damage

params.durationSec: seconds during which autoscaling cannot add units

params.errorRate: share of requests failing on the bad version
params.durationSec: untilFixed; with ci-cd only canaryShare of units run it until rollback
untilFixed; with config-service only its stagedShare is hit first

params.restartSec: seconds of half capacity on every compute element while keys are rotated by redeploy; zero impact with secrets-manager

events.name: Viral spike
events.description: A post blows up. Traffic climbs to several times normal within minutes.

counters.how: Adds servers, but only after a minute of measuring plus boot time.
Serves popular content without touching your servers.
Keeps repeated reads off the database.
Turns write spikes into a short wait instead of errors.
Headroom: run at about 60 percent busy so you can absorb 1.5 times.

events.lesson: Spikes arrive faster than new servers start. Keep headroom, let caches and CDNs absorb reads, queue what can wait, and autoscale for the rest.

debrief.headline: Viral spike: traffic reached {factor} times normal ({peakRps} req/s).
debrief.hurt: {node} ran out of room for {minutes} minutes and {failed} requests failed.
debrief.fix: Add headroom or a cache in front of {node}, and turn on autoscaling.

events.realWorld: A front-page link can send 10 to 50 times normal traffic within 15 minutes, approx.
events.icon: Upward-curving arrow with three short motion lines below it.

events.name: Flash crowd
events.description: Tickets go on sale, a show premieres or a patch drops. Everyone arrives in the same 30 seconds.

counters.how: A virtual waiting room admits people at a pace the busiest step can handle.
Caps each client so bots cannot take every slot.
Serves the static pages and the waiting room itself.
Scale up before the known start time; autoscaling is too slow for 30 seconds.

events.lesson: When you know when the crowd comes, scale before it arrives and let people in at a steady rate from a waiting room.

debrief.headline: Flash crowd: {factor} times normal in {rampSec} seconds.
debrief.hurt: {failed} requests failed in the first {minutes} minutes while {node} was overwhelmed.
debrief.fix: Pre-scale before the start time and put a waiting-room queue in front of {node}.

events.realWorld: Ticket sales, market opens and enrolment days can bring millions of people within a minute of the start, approx.
events.icon: Cluster of five small person dots rushing toward a narrow door.

events.name: Deadline surge
events.description: Tax day, enrollment close or a sign-up deadline. Traffic climbs for hours until the cut-off.

counters.how: A slow, predictable climb is exactly what autoscaling handles well.
Accept submissions now, process them after the deadline.
Forms and rules pages are the same for everyone.

events.lesson: Predictable surges are the easiest kind: scale on schedule, accept-and-queue the final submissions, and make 'received' the promise, not 'processed'.

debrief.headline: Deadline surge: traffic rose to {factor} times normal over {rampHours} hours.
debrief.hurt: In the last hour, {failed} submissions failed at {node}.
debrief.fix: Accept submissions into a queue and confirm receipt; process them after the deadline.

events.realWorld: Tax filing sites often see several times their normal daily volume on the final day, approx.
events.icon: Calendar page with an upward arrow climbing to its last day.

events.name: Hot key
events.description: One item gets a huge share of traffic: a celebrity profile, one product, one merchant.

counters.how: A cache in front answers the hot item from memory.
Public hot items are served from the edge.
Spreads hot reads, though writes still hit one place.

events.lesson: Sharding spreads keys, not popularity. One hot key still lands on one shard; cache it, copy it, or split it.

debrief.headline: Hot key: {share} percent of traffic hit a single item.
debrief.hurt: The one unit of {node} that held it overloaded while the others sat idle.
debrief.helped: {helper} answered the hot item before it reached storage.
debrief.fix: Put a cache in front of {node}; for hot writes, split the key into several sub-keys.

events.realWorld: A single partition in a managed key-value store tops out around 1,000 writes per second, approx.
events.icon: Key with three small heat lines rising from it.

events.name: Celebrity post
events.description: Someone with 50 million followers posts. Copying it into every follower's feed means 50 million writes.

counters.how: Do the fan-out in the background at a steady pace.
Workers spread the copying over minutes.
Pull celebrity posts at read time instead of copying them.

events.lesson: Fan-out on write is fast to read and expensive for celebrities; fan-out on read is the reverse. Big systems mix both.

debrief.headline: Celebrity post: one write turned into {factor} times the write load.
debrief.hurt: {node} fell behind and feeds were {lagMinutes} minutes late.
debrief.fix: Fan out through a queue, and serve very popular accounts at read time.

events.realWorld: Copying one post to 50 million feeds at 1 million writes per second still takes about a minute, approx.
events.icon: One large dot with many thin lines spraying out to small dots.

events.name: Cache stampede
events.description: The cache empties (restart, purge, mass expiry) and every request rushes to the database at once.

counters.how: One request refills each key while the rest wait.
Only one location asks your servers per item.
More read capacity behind the cache.
Spreading expiry times avoids everything expiring together.

events.lesson: A cache hides how weak the database behind it is. Plan for the moment it is empty.

debrief.headline: Cache stampede: hit rate fell to zero.
debrief.hurt: {node} received {factor} times its normal reads and {failed} requests failed.
debrief.helped: {helper} limited how many misses reached the database.
debrief.fix: Turn on 'collapse misses' and keep database headroom for a cold cache.

events.realWorld: With a 90 percent hit rate, an empty cache sends 10 times the normal load to the database, approx.
events.icon: Lightning bolt broken in the middle, with small arrows pouring downward.

events.name: Database failover
events.description: The primary database dies. A standby takes over after about a minute.

counters.how: A standby in a second zone takes over; with one zone, you wait for a rebuild.
sync replication loses nothing; async loses the last moment of writes.
Holds connections and halves the switchover time.
Writes wait in the queue instead of failing.
Clients that retry with jitter reconnect gently.

events.lesson: Failover is measured in two numbers: how long you were down (RTO) and how much data you lost (RPO). Choose them on purpose.

debrief.headline: Database failover: the primary was down for {seconds} seconds.
debrief.hurt: {failed} requests failed and {lostWrites} acknowledged writes were lost.
debrief.helped: {helper} kept writes safe during the switch.
debrief.fix: Run the database across 2 zones with sync replication, and put a pooler in front.

events.realWorld: Managed database failover typically takes 30 to 120 seconds, approx.
events.icon: Database cylinder with a curved arrow handing over to a second cylinder.

events.name: Replication lag
events.description: Copies fall behind. Users read old data, even their own fresh changes.

counters.how: Read your own recent writes from the primary.
Invalidates caches and indexes as soon as data changes.

events.lesson: Copies are always a little behind. Decide which screens must show the very latest and read those from the source.

debrief.headline: Replication lag: copies fell {lagSec} seconds behind.
debrief.hurt: {stale} reads showed old data, including people's own changes.
debrief.helped: {helper} kept fresh reads on the primary.
debrief.fix: Read-after-write from the primary for a few seconds after a change.

events.realWorld: Replica lag is usually under a second and can reach minutes under heavy writes, approx.
events.icon: Two clocks side by side, the second one's hands behind the first.

events.name: Zone outage
events.description: One data-centre building (an availability zone) loses power or network for an hour.

counters.how: Spread every component across 3 zones.
Run each zone at about 60 percent so the other two can carry the load.

events.lesson: Run in 3 zones at about 60 percent each, so losing one leaves two at 90 percent instead of zero.

debrief.headline: Zone outage: zone {zone} was down for {minutes} minutes.
debrief.hurt: {node} lived only in that zone and went dark.
debrief.helped: {helper} carried on from the other zones.
debrief.fix: Set every stateful component to 2 or 3 zones.

events.realWorld: Zone outages happen a few times a year across the big clouds and often last 1 to 4 hours, approx.
events.icon: Three small buildings in a row, the middle one crossed out.

events.name: Region outage
events.description: A whole cloud region goes down for a couple of hours.

counters.how: Sends users to the surviving region in about 90 seconds.
Sends users to the surviving region in about 30 seconds.
Brings up a standby; speed depends on the mode.
Copies in another region mean data survives.

events.lesson: Multi-region is a business decision: hours of downtime and cheap, or minutes and double the cost.

debrief.headline: Region outage: {region} was down for {minutes} minutes.
debrief.hurt: Users were cut off for {downMinutes} minutes and {lostWrites} writes were lost.
debrief.fix: Add a second region behind GeoDNS or a global load balancer, or a disaster-recovery plan.

events.realWorld: Full region outages are rare, about once every year or two per provider, and can last hours, approx.
events.icon: Globe with one continent shaded and crossed out.

events.name: Slow dependency
events.description: An outside service slows from 150 ms to 3 seconds. Your servers fill with requests waiting on it.

counters.how: Give up after 300 ms to 1 s instead of waiting 30 s.
Stops calling it and fails fast for a while.
Call it in the background so users do not wait.
Serve the last good answer.

events.lesson: Slow is worse than down: waiting requests hold servers hostage. Set short timeouts and fail fast.

debrief.headline: Slow dependency: {node} took {addLatencyMs} ms extra.
debrief.hurt: Callers waited up to {timeoutMs} ms per call, lost {capacityLostPct} percent of their capacity, and {failed} requests failed.
debrief.fix: Set a 1 second timeout and add a circuit breaker in front of {node}.

events.realWorld: A server that can do 1,000 rps at 50 ms does about 17 rps when each request waits 3 s, approx.
events.icon: Snail shell shape next to a small clock.

events.name: Dependency outage
events.description: An outside service (payments, email, maps, an AI model) fails every call for 20 minutes.

counters.how: Accept now, finish when it is back ('payment pending').
Retries the step later without losing the order.
Fails fast instead of piling up.
Falls back to a second model provider.

events.lesson: Every outside service will fail sometimes. Decide in advance what your product does then: queue, degrade, or switch providers.

debrief.headline: Dependency outage: {node} was down for {minutes} minutes.
debrief.hurt: {failed} {types} failed outright.
debrief.helped: {helper} held the work until it returned.
debrief.fix: Queue calls to {node} and retry them later; tell users 'pending' instead of 'failed'.

events.realWorld: A provider at 99.95 percent availability is down about 22 minutes a month, approx.
events.icon: Puzzle piece with a crack and a small x.

events.name: Retry storm
events.description: A half-minute blip fails most requests; every client retries at once, up to three times, and the load roughly quadruples.

counters.how: Exponential backoff with jitter spreads retries out.
Fewer retries mean less amplification.
Caps the flood per client.
Stops hammering a struggling service.

events.lesson: Retries without backoff turn a small problem into a big one: 3 retries can mean 4 times the load exactly when you are weakest.

debrief.headline: Retry storm: a short blip at {node} grew into {factor} times the load.
debrief.hurt: Retries kept {node} overloaded for {minutes} minutes after the blip ended.
debrief.fix: Use exponential backoff with jitter and at most 2 retries.

events.realWorld: Several well-known multi-hour outages were prolonged by clients retrying in lockstep, approx.
events.icon: Three circular arrows stacked, each larger than the last.

events.name: Thundering herd
events.description: After a restart or outage, every client reconnects and signs in at the same moment.

counters.how: Random jitter spreads reconnects over a minute.
Admits reconnects at a safe pace.
Serves session and profile reads.

events.lesson: Recovery is a spike of its own. Spread reconnects with random delays.

debrief.headline: Thundering herd: {factor} times normal reconnects in {rampSec} seconds.
debrief.hurt: {node} was knocked over again right after recovering.
debrief.fix: Add random jitter to reconnects and a rate limiter in front of sign-in.

events.realWorld: A million clients reconnecting within 10 seconds is 100,000 connections per second, approx.
events.icon: Many small arrows converging on one point from all sides.

events.name: Cost blowout
events.description: A crawler hits uncached pages all day, and every pay-per-use part of the bill multiplies.

counters.how: Cached answers cost a fraction of origin answers.
One crawler cannot take thousands of pages a second.
Blocks known bad bots.
A budget alert catches it in hours, not at month end.

events.lesson: Pay-per-use is cheap until something uses it a lot. Cache, limit, and alert on spend.

debrief.headline: Cost blowout: usage costs ran {factor} times normal for {hours} hours.
debrief.hurt: The month's bill rose by about ${costDelta}.
debrief.fix: Cache what bots read and rate-limit per client; add a spend alert.

events.realWorld: Runaway serverless or egress bills of thousands of dollars in a weekend are a common story, approx.
events.icon: Dollar coin with an upward arrow bursting from it.

events.name: Compliance audit
events.description: An auditor checks your design: who did what, encryption keys, personal data, backups and consent.

counters.how: Proves who did what and when.
Shows data is encrypted with managed keys.
Keeps personal data in one controlled place.
Shows you can restore.
Shows every access is signed in.
Shows you honour opt-outs.

events.lesson: Regulated industries (health, money, government) need proof built into the design, not added at audit time.

debrief.headline: Compliance audit: {passed} of {total} checks passed.
debrief.hurt: Missing: {missing}.
debrief.fix: Add the missing pieces: {missing}.

events.realWorld: Health, payment-card and finance rules each require audit trails, encryption and tested backups, approx.
events.icon: Clipboard with a magnifying glass over a check mark.

events.name: DDoS attack
events.description: A botnet floods you with 50 times your peak traffic in junk requests.

counters.how: Absorbs the flood at the network edge.
Huge edge capacity soaks up much of it.
Blocks junk web requests.
Caps each source.

events.lesson: You cannot out-scale a botnet. Filter at the edge, in layers, before traffic reaches anything you pay for per request.

debrief.headline: DDoS attack: {factor} times your peak in junk traffic.
debrief.hurt: Junk reached {node} and crowded out {failed} real requests.
debrief.fix: Put a DDoS shield and WAF in front, and a CDN to absorb the rest.

events.realWorld: Large attacks now exceed a few terabits per second and tens of millions of requests per second, approx.
events.icon: Many small x marks raining onto a shield.

events.name: Bot scraping
events.description: Bots try stolen passwords and scrape every page, at half your normal traffic, all day.

counters.how: Bot rules recognise scrapers and stuffers.
Limits attempts per client.
Lockouts and two-factor stop stolen passwords.

events.lesson: Not all traffic is human. Count bots in your capacity plan and filter them early.

debrief.headline: Bot scraping: bots added {factor} times your peak in sign-ins and reads.
debrief.hurt: {node} spent {wastePct} percent of its capacity on bots.
debrief.fix: Add a WAF with bot rules and a per-client rate limit.

events.realWorld: Automated bots make up roughly a third to a half of web traffic, approx.
events.icon: Small robot head with a magnifying glass.

events.name: Bad deploy
events.description: A new version ships with a bug; 30 percent of requests to that service fail.

counters.how: A 5 percent canary limits the damage, and rollback takes about 5 minutes.
Switch the new code path off in seconds.
Notices the error rate in minutes.
Gets a person on it quickly.

events.lesson: Most outages start with a change. Ship small, canary first, watch, and make rollback one click.

debrief.headline: Bad deploy at {node}: {errorPct} percent of its requests failed.
debrief.hurt: It took {minutes} minutes to notice and roll back; {failed} requests failed.
debrief.fix: Add a CI/CD pipeline with a canary and quick rollback, plus alerting.

events.realWorld: Industry studies consistently find most incidents follow a change such as a deploy or config edit, approx.
events.icon: Package box with a small crack and a warning mark.

events.name: Bad config push
events.description: A bad setting reaches every server at once. Everything starts failing together.

counters.how: Staged rollout hits 10 percent first and keeps the last good config.
Kill switch for the affected behaviour.
Catches a total failure within a minute.

events.lesson: Config is code. Roll it out in stages, validate it, and keep the last good version ready.

debrief.headline: Bad config push: {errorPct} percent of requests failed everywhere at once.
debrief.hurt: Outage lasted {minutes} minutes.
debrief.helped: {helper} contained it to a slice of servers.
debrief.fix: Push config through a staged config service that keeps the last good version.

events.realWorld: Several of the largest public cloud and CDN outages were caused by a single global config change, approx.
events.icon: Three sliders with one knob pushed to the far end and a warning mark.

events.name: Noisy neighbour
events.description: A big report or batch job runs on the live database at noon and takes half its capacity.

counters.how: Run reports on a replica, not the primary.
Analytics belongs in the warehouse.
Per-tenant limits stop one customer taking everything.

events.lesson: Separate heavy, slow work from live user traffic: different copies, different machines, different limits.

debrief.headline: Noisy neighbour: {node} lost half its capacity to a heavy job.
debrief.hurt: Live requests slowed to {p99} ms at p99 and {failed} failed.
debrief.helped: {helper} kept heavy work away from live traffic.
debrief.fix: Point reports at a replica or the warehouse.

events.realWorld: One unindexed report can use all of a database's CPU for minutes, approx.
events.icon: Two houses side by side, one with loud sound waves coming out.

events.name: Memory leak
events.description: A service slowly loses memory and gets slower each hour until someone restarts it.

counters.how: Shows memory climbing.
Fires before it hurts users.
Replaces unhealthy servers with fresh ones.

events.lesson: Slow problems hide in averages. Watch saturation, not only errors.

debrief.headline: Memory leak at {node}: capacity fell {pct} percent per hour.
debrief.hurt: It went unnoticed for {minutes} minutes.
debrief.fix: Add metrics with alerting on memory, and let health checks replace bad servers.

events.realWorld: Leaks often take hours or days to show and are found by watching memory graphs, approx.
events.icon: Water droplet falling from a memory stick.

events.name: Disk full
events.description: Data or logs fill the disk. Writes stop until someone frees space.

counters.how: Keep only what you need.
Alert on growth rate days before it is full.
Writes wait instead of failing.

events.lesson: Storage fills predictably. Alert on how fast it grows, and set retention from day one.

debrief.headline: Disk full: {node} stopped accepting writes.
debrief.hurt: {failed} writes failed over {minutes} minutes.
debrief.fix: Set retention and alert when the disk will be full within 3 days.

events.realWorld: Disk-full incidents are among the most common and most preventable outages, approx.
events.icon: Hard drive with a level gauge at the top of its scale.

events.name: Cold starts
events.description: A burst needs new serverless instances; each new one takes almost a second to start.

counters.how: Keep some instances ready.
Always-on containers have no cold start.

events.lesson: Pay-per-use compute starts from zero. Keep a few warm for latency-sensitive paths.

debrief.headline: Cold starts added {addMs} ms to new instances.
debrief.hurt: p99 latency rose to {p99} ms during the burst.
debrief.fix: Keep a warm pool sized for your typical burst.

events.realWorld: Function cold starts range from about 100 ms to over 1 second depending on language and size, approx.
events.icon: Snowflake beside a small lightning bolt.

events.name: Poison message
events.description: One malformed message crashes every worker that picks it up, again and again.

counters.how: After 5 failures the message is parked and work resumes.
Fires when the queue stops draining.

events.lesson: Never let one bad message block the line. Cap retries and park failures.

debrief.headline: Poison message in {node}.
debrief.hurt: Workers processed nothing for {minutes} minutes; {backlog} messages piled up.
debrief.fix: Connect a dead-letter queue to {node}.

events.realWorld: Without a retry cap, one bad message can stall a pipeline indefinitely, approx.
events.icon: Envelope with a small hazard triangle on its corner.

events.name: Duplicate delivery
events.description: The queue redelivers 1 percent of messages. Without protection, some customers are charged twice.

counters.how: Recognises the repeat and skips it.
Deduplicates published events.
Unique posting ids reject a second copy.

events.lesson: Most queues deliver at least once, not exactly once. Make every handler safe to run twice.

debrief.headline: Duplicate delivery: {share} percent of messages arrived twice.
debrief.hurt: {duplicates} duplicate {types} went through.
debrief.fix: Check an idempotency key before every money move or side effect.

events.realWorld: Standard managed queues guarantee at-least-once delivery; duplicates are rare but certain at scale, approx.
events.icon: Two identical envelopes overlapping.

events.name: Network partition
events.description: Your regions cannot talk to each other for 5 minutes.

counters.how: Stays correct: the minority side stops writing.
Holds cross-region work until the link returns.

events.lesson: During a partition you choose: refuse some requests to stay correct, or accept them and reconcile later.

debrief.headline: Network partition for {minutes} minutes.
debrief.hurt: {failed} requests were refused, or {conflicts} conflicting writes need fixing.
debrief.fix: Pick per feature: money stays consistent, likes and views stay available.

events.realWorld: Cross-region links fail or degrade for minutes a few times a year, approx.
events.icon: Two circles with a zigzag break between them.

events.name: Certificate expired
events.description: The HTTPS certificate on your front door expires. Every browser refuses to connect.

counters.how: Notices within a minute.
Gets someone to renew it fast.

events.lesson: Automate renewals and check expiry from outside. This one is always avoidable.

debrief.headline: Certificate expired on {node}.
debrief.hurt: Every request failed for {minutes} minutes.
debrief.fix: Automatic renewal plus a synthetic check on expiry date.

events.realWorld: Expired certificates have taken down major apps and services for hours, approx.
events.icon: Certificate ribbon with a small clock showing zero.

events.name: DNS mistake
events.description: A wrong DNS record sends half your users nowhere, and caches keep the mistake for an hour.

counters.how: A short TTL means mistakes expire in a minute.
Catches it from outside.

events.lesson: Lower the TTL before changing DNS, so you can undo a mistake quickly.

debrief.headline: DNS mistake: half of users got a wrong address.
debrief.hurt: The wrong answer stayed cached for {minutes} minutes.
debrief.fix: Lower TTL to 60 s before changes.

events.realWorld: Common DNS TTLs are 5 minutes to 1 hour; some resolvers keep answers longer, approx.
events.icon: Signpost with its arrow board pointing the wrong way and a small x.

events.name: Provider rate limit
events.description: An outside service starts answering 'too many requests' above half your current rate.

counters.how: Send at the allowed pace and let the rest wait.
Do not ask twice for the same answer.
Back off when told to.

events.lesson: Know your providers' limits before launch day, and design to stay under them.

debrief.headline: {node} limited you to {cap} req/s.
debrief.hurt: {failed} calls were refused.
debrief.fix: Queue calls to {node} and send at its limit; cache repeated answers.

events.realWorld: Many APIs default to about 100 requests per second per account until you ask for more, approx.
events.icon: Gauge with its needle at a red line and a hand-stop sign.

events.name: Bad migration
events.description: A buggy data change damages 5 percent of rows, and replicas faithfully copy the damage.

counters.how: Point-in-time restore to 5 minutes before the change.
Migration checks catch it in testing.

events.lesson: Replicas protect against machines failing, not against mistakes. Only backups undo a bad change.

debrief.headline: Bad migration damaged {share} percent of {node}.
debrief.hurt: {lostWrites} records were wrong; restore took {minutes} minutes.
debrief.fix: Turn on point-in-time backups and test restores.

events.realWorld: Restoring a database snapshot takes roughly an hour per terabyte, approx.
events.icon: Database cylinder with a jagged crack across it.

events.name: Metrics explosion
events.description: Someone adds a user id to a metric label. Series count jumps 20 times and so does the bill.

counters.how: An alert on series count catches it in minutes.

events.lesson: Labels must have few possible values. Put ids in logs or traces, never in metric labels.

debrief.headline: Metrics explosion: series count rose {factor} times.
debrief.hurt: Monitoring cost rose by about ${costDelta} for the month.
debrief.fix: Limit labels per metric and alert on active series.

events.realWorld: At about $0.10 to $0.30 per 1,000 series a month, 20 million accidental series cost thousands, approx.
events.icon: Small line chart exploding into many thin lines.

events.name: Leaked key
events.description: An API key is pushed to a public repo. It must be rotated now.

counters.how: Rotate in minutes with no redeploy.
Keys can be disabled instantly.

events.lesson: Assume secrets leak. Keep them out of code so rotating is boring.

debrief.headline: Leaked key had to be rotated.
debrief.hurt: Redeploying every service halved capacity for {minutes} minutes.
debrief.fix: Store keys in a secrets manager.

events.realWorld: Automated scanners find keys pushed to public code within minutes, approx.
events.icon: Key slipping out of an open padlock.

events.name: GPU shortage
events.description: Demand for AI jumps, and the cloud has no more GPUs to give you for two hours.

counters.how: Answers repeated questions without a GPU.
Overflows to a hosted model.
Lets long jobs wait their turn.

events.lesson: GPUs are scarce and slow to add. Plan fallbacks: cache, a smaller model, or a hosted provider.

debrief.headline: GPU shortage: AI demand rose {factor} times with no new GPUs.
debrief.hurt: Replies queued for up to {waitSec} seconds and {failed} timed out.
debrief.fix: Add a semantic cache and a gateway that can fall back to a hosted model.

events.realWorld: High-end GPUs have often been sold out in popular regions for days, approx.
events.icon: GPU chip with an empty box outline beside it.

events.name: Table lock
events.description: A schema change locks a busy table. Writes wait for 3 minutes.

counters.how: Writes wait in the queue instead of timing out.
Runs online migrations in small steps.

events.lesson: Change schemas in small, online steps: add, backfill, switch, then remove.

debrief.headline: Table lock on {node} for {minutes} minutes.
debrief.hurt: {failed} writes timed out.
debrief.fix: Use online migrations and buffer writes through a queue.

events.realWorld: Some table changes on large tables lock writes for minutes unless done online, approx.
events.icon: Table grid with a padlock over its corner.

events.name: Overseas launch
events.description: Marketing launches in a new continent. 40 percent of users are now far from your servers.

counters.how: Serves static and cached content locally.
Runs light logic near users.
Routes them to a second region near them.

events.lesson: Distance is latency: about 150 to 300 ms per round trip across oceans, and pages need several round trips.

debrief.headline: Overseas launch: {share} percent of users moved to {region}.
debrief.hurt: Their p99 latency rose to {p99} ms.
debrief.fix: Put a CDN in front and consider a second region.

events.realWorld: A round trip from the US east coast to Singapore is about 220 ms, approx.
events.icon: Airplane above a globe with a dotted path.
